description: Figure 5 presents an error analysis comparison between two pie charts, one for the Vanilla model (left) and one for the HCL model (right), showing how outcomes are distributed across four categories; each pie chart contains 4 slices with percentage labels inside the slices and a shared legend above the pies. In the Vanilla model pie (left), the largest slice is labeled “Correct” and is shown in a dark teal color at approximately 68.0%, followed by “Reason Error” in a medium blue at about 12.0%, “Question Misunderstood” in a light gray at about 12.0%, and “Atomic Skill Fail” in a lighter teal at about 8.0%. In the HCL model pie (right), the largest slice is “Correct” in dark teal at approximately 55.0%, with the remaining slices labeled “Question Misunderstood” in light gray at about 21.0%, “Reason Error” in medium blue at about 14.0%, and “Atomic Skill Fail” in lighter teal at about 10.0%. Neither pie appears exploded or otherwise visually emphasized, and the slices do not appear to be arranged strictly in descending order.
